# SAM 3.1 chatbot-GUI fit spike

## Context

The user asks how Meta SAM 3.1 (vision segmentation model) fits the planned GUI where the chatbot loads and renders the full GUI, following the earlier question of feeding SAM the raw json-render output of the incoming schema/start stream. Intended end state: a time-boxed, read-only spike that (a) corrects the render premise against the repo docs, (b) runs SAM 3.1 once against real rendered pixels derived from a real json-render spec stream, and (c) reports with evidence where SAM fits (post-render visual grounding) or does not fit (raw JSON is not a SAM input). No platform, catalog, mount, or EMQX changes.

## Approach

1. Premise check, read-only (30 min cap). Re-read `docs/DROP-IN-SPEC.md` sections 1-3 and `docs/DEV-CYCLE.md` UI rows, plus `SPARK-BRIEF.md` avatar/chat-path lines. Record one inline verdict: the chatbot does NOT render the GUI in the docs; the sole rendering engine is json-render through its Svelte renderer (`@json-render/svelte` `Renderer`), with the team-chat target as a mapping of the same spec — never a second renderer, never the chatbot, never SAM. The chatbot answers via the chat path and co-signs by policy; the avatar speaks a fixed intro. SAM therefore cannot sit between the spec stream and the renderer and cannot render anything; its only candidate slot is after pixels exist. If a doc states otherwise, quote file:line and follow the doc over this plan.

2. Capture one real spec-stream sample, no new code. Use the existing stream APIs documented in `ui/reference/docs/json-render-core.README.md` (`createSpecStreamCompiler`, `compileSpecStream`, `parseSpecStreamLine`): take one checked-in spec (prefer a small page under `/srv/git/3tched.com` references or `operation-dashboard-ui-07/specs/`) and its stream-line form. Save the exact input files used as `local/sam-spike/input-spec.json` and `local/sam-spike/input-stream.jsonl` (both gitignored via `local/`). Do not invent a synthetic schema; do not write to any mount, SHM path, or broker topic.

3. Render the sample to pixels with the sole engine only, no model. Render exclusively via json-render's Svelte renderer (`Renderer` + catalog validation from `@json-render/core`) against the sealed catalog, producing `local/sam-spike/render.png` at a fixed viewport (1280x800). No `schema_renderer` path, no team-chat mapping, no screenshot substitution for the valid path. Record renderer name (`@json-render/svelte` `Renderer`), catalog/schema hash, and viewport in the report. This step is load-bearing: SAM 3.1 takes images, not JSON text; feeding raw JSON lines directly into SAM is a type error and the spike must demonstrate the failure mode once (one raw-text attempt logged as rejected/nonsense) plus the valid image path.

4. Resolve the SAM 3.1 artifact, then run inference once, local only. First list local checkpoints (`ls ~/.cache/huggingface /srv/models /tmp 2>/dev/null`) and record the exact checkpoint path or HuggingFace id actually used (e.g. local `sam3.1*.pt` if present). Run a minimal throwaway harness at `local/sam-spike/run_sam.py` (stdlib plus whichever SAM runner the checkpoint supports; no repo changes, no network beyond model weights if already cached). Input is strictly `local/sam-spike/render.png`; output is `local/sam-spike/masks.json` (boxes/masks/scores) plus `local/sam-spike/annotated.png`. No 8090 calls, no EMQX, no mount writes.

5. Map masks back to spec elements and decide fit. Join `masks.json` regions to the flat `elements` keys of `input-spec.json` by bounding-box overlap against the renderer's layout (reuse element keys, never rename). Write `local/sam-spike/fit-report.md` with: (a) the premise verdict from step 1, (b) the raw-JSON attempt outcome, (c) a per-element table (element key, type, matched mask id or none, IoU/overlap note), and (d) a single fit verdict: SAM fits only as an optional post-render grounder (click targets, visual QA, accessibility boxes) behind the sealed spec, never as a spec consumer, renderer, or authority. If overlap is unusable, verdict is does-not-fit with the numbers, not a tuning loop.

6. Stop. Leave all spike outputs under gitignored `local/sam-spike/`; do not copy anything into `docs/`, `book/`, `schema/`, or the platform repo. Report the verdict plus file paths in chat.
## Critical files & anchors

- `docs/DROP-IN-SPEC.md` sections 1-3 (generator pipeline, 2.1 renderer targets, 2.2 governed actions, section 3 thin adapters) — why the chatbot is not the renderer.
- `docs/DEV-CYCLE.md` UI rows (screens from sealed plugin schemas, specs validated against the catalog before shown) — sole-engine rule: json-render Svelte renderer only.
- `ui/reference/docs/json-render-core.README.md` around `createSpecStreamCompiler` / `compileSpecStream` / `parseSpecStreamLine` — the real stream/start APIs to sample.
- `/srv/git/odbus-verified/crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/json_render.rs` `PLUGIN_NAME` / `PLUGIN_VERSION` region — sealed method inventory the sample must come from.
- `SPARK-BRIEF.md` avatar + chat-path lines — chatbot answers via chat path, avatar fixed intro.
## Verification

- `ls local/sam-spike/` shows exactly `input-spec.json`, `input-stream.jsonl`, `render.png`, `masks.json`, `annotated.png`, `fit-report.md`, `run_sam.py`; `git status --short` in `/srv/git/etched-in-schema` shows no tracked changes.
- Open `local/sam-spike/annotated.png`: mask overlays align to visible UI regions from `render.png`; open `fit-report.md`: per-element table names real element keys from `input-spec.json` with matched or explicitly unmatched masks.
- Negative check recorded in the report: the one raw-JSON-text-into-SAM attempt with its observed outcome (rejected or nonsense), proving raw spec text is not a valid SAM input.
- No receipts created, no mount/SHM/broker writes performed (nothing to show because the spike performs none; any such write fails the spike).

## Assumptions & contingencies

- Assumes SAM 3.1 means the Meta vision segmentation model and the GUI premise is the chatbot-loaded full GUI; confirmed via user selection this turn. If the artifact cannot be resolved locally (no checkpoint, no cached weights, no network to fetch), do not substitute another model: record artifact-unavailable, keep steps 1-3 plus the raw-JSON negative check, and verdict remains valid on architecture alone.
- If no checked-in spec renders deterministically (renderer or catalog unavailable), fall back to a screenshot of the live reference UI at the same fixed viewport, recorded as screenshot-not-spec-render in the report; do not hand-author a spec.
- If mask-*** overlap is meaningless, verdict is does-not-fit with numbers; do not add tuning, training, or a second model pass.
